Question: How can God declare sinners righteous and still be just?
ShortAnswer: God can declare sinners righteous because their sins were fully punished in Christ, and Christ's righteousness is credited to them. Paul calls this the heart of the gospel: God is 'just and the one who justifies those who have faith in Jesus' (Romans 3:26).
DetailedAnswer: This is the sharpest question in the Bible, and Paul spends Romans 1-3 building up to it. If a human judge declared a guilty criminal righteous and let him walk free, we would call it corruption. How can God do it and remain just? The answer is that God does not wave sin away — He deals with it. Isaiah pictured a servant who would bear the iniquities of others (Isaiah 53:11), and Paul says God made Christ, who had no sin, 'to be sin for us, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God' (2 Corinthians 5:21). On the cross, Jesus took the penalty our sins deserved; in return, His perfect righteousness is credited — imputed — to everyone who trusts in Him. That is why Paul can say we are 'justified freely by his grace through the redemption that came by Christ Jesus' (Romans 3:24) and 'have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ' (Romans 5:1). Justification is a legal declaration, not a fiction: it rests on a real punishment borne and a real righteousness given. God remains just because sin was punished; sinners go free because it was punished in Christ, not in them.
